name: Trade war & tariffs
summary: Trump's 12 Nov threat to double tariffs on Mexican goods over a migrant caravan stands; no increase in force by 14 Nov
state: On 12 Nov President Trump threatened to double tariffs on Mexican goods, including steel, aluminium and vehicles, unless Mexico stops a caravan of more than 1,000 migrants that left Tapachula on 10 Nov (Mexico News Daily, 14 Nov). President Sheinbaum said Mexico would not use force against migrants; no tariff increase had taken effect by 14 Nov. Sheinbaum travels to APEC in Shenzhen on 17–19 Nov, where Trump and Xi are also due to meet. Watch holds: a major tariff rise has been threatened but not imposed.
for_you: Exporters, importers and manufacturers trading with the US, Mexico and China are most exposed to sudden tariff changes, which tend to feed through to prices and supply chains over months. UK firms can check GOV.UK guidance on US tariffs.
rubric_hit: Watch: major tariff increase threatened between large economies (US on Mexico, 12 Nov); not in force

sources.title: Mexico News Daily — Mexico's week in review: Trump renews tariff threats as Sheinbaum prepares for China

why: Tariffs raise prices, reroute supply chains and slow growth; escalation cycles hurt export-heavy economies like the UK's partners.
drivers: US tariff policy, retaliation, court rulings, trade deals, WTO disputes.

rubric.alert: Broad new tariffs in force with retaliation under way, or US average effective tariff rising sharply.
rubric.watch: New major tariffs announced or threatened between large economies.
rubric.normal: Tariff regime stable; no new major measures in the past two weeks.
